conceptual assets.information: The channel-selection decision determines which repeated PWM channel receives a bus write or supplies a read. It has no direct entry or exit port because the bus address only decides this internal select.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address-derived select can steer a write or read to a different channel, so its integrity can be violated through the selection logic at line 109. It can also make an access miss every channel and lose a required configuration transfer when no channel matches, because the select gates the channel strobes at lines 109-111.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can issue a request with a changed or invalid address so that configuration is applied to the wrong channel or to no channel.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable setting determines whether a PWM channel runs and whether its clock request is asserted. PWM operation depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The enable is sensitive control configuration that a bus write can modify through the channel register at lines 183-184. Clearing it resets the PWM timing state and forces the channel inactive at lines 212-234, so it can block operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can write a zero enable value to disable a channel and prevent its PWM output from operating.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler setting selects which clock-generator timing bit advances the PWM divider. The selected rate determines the timing of the generated waveform.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The prescaler is configuration material that a bus write can change at line 185, and the changed value selects the timing input used at line 214, altering PWM timing.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can overwrite the prescaler so that the PWM waveform runs at an unintended timing rate.

conceptual assets.information: The polarity setting determines whether the active portion of each PWM waveform is represented by a high or low output level. The output behavior depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The polarity is sensitive output configuration that a bus write can modify at line 186, and it directly selects the output level at lines 232-234.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can overwrite the polarity setting and invert the externally observed PWM control signal.

conceptual assets.information: The period-divider setting determines how many selected clock-generator events occur between PWM timing ticks. The generated PWM period depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The period-divider configuration can be modified by bus data at line 187, and it controls the divider rollover and tick generation at lines 215-220, changing the PWM period.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can overwrite the period divider to produce a PWM frequency different from the intended one.

conceptual assets.information: The duty-cycle setting determines the threshold used to form the active portion of each PWM period. The waveform duty cycle depends on this setting.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The duty-cycle configuration can be modified by bus data at line 188, and it is compared with the duty counter to choose the PWM output at line 231.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can overwrite the duty setting to change the proportion of each PWM period for which the output is active.

conceptual assets.information: The aggregate clock-enable request tells the surrounding clock generator whether any PWM channel requires its timing source. PWM generation depends on the surrounding clock remaining enabled when a channel is active.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The aggregate control output is produced by reducing the channel enable outputs at line 121, so an incorrect channel-enable state can corrupt the clock request. Withholding or deasserting this request can stop the timing source needed by enabled PWM channels, creating an availability failure at line 121.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can cause the aggregate clock-enable request to remain low, preventing the clock generator from supplying timing to the PWM channels.

conceptual assets.information: The PWM waveform is the per-channel control signal produced for external loads or devices. Correct operation depends on the channel enable, polarity, period and duty settings.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The waveform is a sensitive externally used control output whose value is selected by the configuration and duty comparison at lines 231-234, while bus writes can alter those settings at lines 183-188. Disabling a channel forces its output inactive and prevents normal PWM operation at lines 212-234.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker can modify the channel configuration to invert, distort or suppress the PWM waveform delivered at the output.
